# The display kit (`dist/display/`)

The kit's look, words and parts for the 480 x 320 workshop display (display-kit spec K1 to K9). Header-only C++17: include
`display/ui.h`. Nothing here depends on a graphics library. The parts draw through **`UiCanvas`**, which the display
repo implements once over LovyanGFX; the kit's own tests implement it over an in-memory RGB565 buffer
(`tests/display/mem_canvas.h`), so every part is rendered and checked on a Mac.

```
dist/tokens.h      UI_COLOR_* (RGB565), UI_FS_*, UI_R_*     the parts include "../tokens.h"
dist/words.h       UI_WORD_*, UI_TEXT_*, UI_AGE_*             the state words, control words and age rules (K4)
dist/needs.h       UI_NEED_*, UI_NEED_PHRASES                 the Needs-you phrases (K4)
dist/display/      ui.h and the parts, fonts.h, fonts/*.vlw
```

No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI needed; strings are `const char*` (UTF-8) owned by the caller; the parts copy into small
stack buffers (160 bytes for fitted text). Only colours from `tokens.h` are used: a part never takes a raw `0x....`.

## The adapter: `UiCanvas`

```cpp
enum class UiFont : uint8_t { Fs3, Fs4, Fs5, Fs6, Readout };  // 14, 16, 20, 26 px; Readout 34 px at 75% width

class UiCanvas {
 public:
  virtual ~UiCanvas() = default;
  virtual void fillRect(int x, int y, int w, int h, uint16_t color) = 0;
  virtual void fillRoundRect(int x, int y, int w, int h, int r, uint16_t color) = 0;
  virtual void line(int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, uint16_t color) = 0;
  virtual void text(int x, int baseline, const char* utf8, UiFont font, uint16_t fg, uint16_t bg) = 0;
  virtual int textWidth(const char* utf8, UiFont font) = 0;
};
```

- Colours are RGB565. Coordinates are pixels from the top left of the 480 x 320 panel; draws past the edge are clipped.
- `fillRoundRect` with `r = w/2 = h/2` is a disc; the parts draw rings and pills from these. Corners need not be
  antialiased (the Mac renders aren't).
- `line` is one pixel wide, both ends included. Thicker strokes (the check mark, the Back chevron) are several lines.
- `text` draws left to right with the first glyph's origin at `x` **on the baseline `baseline`** (LovyanGFX:
  `baseline_left`), not at the top of the line. `fg` is antialiased against `bg`, which is what is already behind it:
  set the text colours to the pair and draw without reading the panel back. Strings are UTF-8; the fonts cover Latin only.
- `textWidth` is the advance of the same string, as `text` lays it out.
- One `UiFont` is one VLW file. The adapter loads the five once (`fonts/archivo-14.vlw`, `-16`, `-20`, `-26`,
  `archivo-readout-34.vlw`; names and byte sizes are in `fonts.h`) and maps the enum to them. In LovyanGFX a `.vlw` loads
  from a file system with `loadFont(path)` or from a byte array with `loadFont(const uint8_t*)`. The kit does not embed
  them as C arrays.

## Shared types (`reading.h`, `canvas.h`)

```cpp
namespace ui {
struct Rect { int x, y, w, h; /* right(), bottom(), contains(px, py), inset(d) */ };
constexpr int kScreenW = 480, kScreenH = 320, kTarget = 48, kGap = 8, kHeaderH = 48, kTabBarH = 48;

enum class ReadingState : uint8_t { Live, Stale, Unavailable, NeverRead };
struct Reading {                       // K6: what a part shows, and how far to trust it
  const char* value;  const char* unit;  uint32_t observedAt;  ReadingState state;
  static Reading live(value, observedAt, unit = nullptr);   static Reading stale(value, observedAt, unit = nullptr);
  static Reading unavailable();        static Reading neverRead();   // a default Reading is never read
  bool known() const;                  // Live or Stale, with a value
  bool live() const;                   // Live, with a value: the only case a lamp may be ok, warn or bad
};
enum class Tone : uint8_t { Ok, Warn, Bad };                  // what a live value means
enum class ChipKind : uint8_t { Ok, Warn, Bad, Unknown };
constexpr ChipKind statusOf(const Reading&, Tone);            // Unknown unless the reading is live

struct Clock { uint32_t epoch; int32_t utcOffsetSeconds; bool set() const; };  // epoch 0: no time yet, ages say Unknown
size_t ageText(char* out, size_t n, uint32_t observedAt, const Clock&);   // "now", "4 min ago", "since 10:32", "since 3 Nov"
size_t sinceText(char* out, size_t n, uint32_t at, const Clock&);         // always "since ..."
bool needPhrase(char* out, size_t n, const char* key, const char* source); // "judge_it" -> "Judge it"; {name} -> source
}
```

**There is no way to draw an unknown reading as ok.** Every part that shows a value takes a `Reading`. Unless it is
`Live` with a value, the part draws the hollow unknown lamp and the word "Unknown" (or the old value in muted text with
its age), whatever `Tone` it was asked for. Ages are the web's words (`words.h`): "now" under a minute, "N min ago"
under an hour, then "since HH:MM" today or "since D Mon" earlier (24-hour). Time is passed in (`Clock`); the kit never
reads a clock.

## Parts

Each is a struct of static functions or a small object with `draw` and a hit-test; hit-tests take the same `Rect` as
`draw` and are pure, so the screen code does `if (Button::hit(r, enabled, x, y)) ...`. Backgrounds (`bg`) must be the
one the part is drawn on: `UI_COLOR_BG`, `UI_COLOR_SURFACE` or `UI_COLOR_SURFACE_2`, the three `docs/contrast.md` measures.

| Part | API | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Chip** (K5) | `Chip::draw(c, x, y, ChipKind, word, live, bg)` returns its width; `Chip::width(c, word, kind)`; `Chip::kHeight` 28 | A dot and its word on an 18% tint of the lamp colour. `live` adds a halo (not for unknown). Unknown is a hollow dot. A null word gets the kind's default (Up, Waiting, Down, Unknown): a chip never has no word. |
| **Button** (K5) | `Button::draw(c, rect, label, ButtonStyle::Primary or Plain, enabled)`; `Button::bounds(rect)`; `Button::width(c, label)`; `Button::hit(rect, enabled, x, y)` | At least 48 x 48: a smaller `rect` is grown from its top left, and `hit` tests the grown area. Primary is the accent fill (one per panel); plain is the well with a `fieldLine` border; disabled has a muted label and no border colour. Lay buttons out 8 px apart. |
| **AgeLine** (K5, K6) | `AgeLine::draw(c, x, baseline, reading, clock, bg)` returns its width; `AgeLine::text(...)` | 14 px. Live ages are muted; anything else is in the unknown colour. |
| **Faceplate** (K5, K6) | `Faceplate::draw(c, rect, caption, reading, tone, word, halo, clock)`; `Faceplate::kMinHeight` 124 | The screen's one panel: caption and lamp across the top, the value in the readout face with its unit, the age. Not live: the lamp is the unknown one saying "Unknown", a missing value reads "Unknown", a stale value stays in muted text. |
| **LampRow** (K5, K6) | `LampRow{label, reading, tone, action}`; `.draw(c, rect, clock, bg)`; `.actionRect(c, rect)`; `.hitAction(c, rect, x, y)`; `LampRow::kHeight` 56 | Lamp, label, value, and at most one action (a plain button, 48 px high, 8 px from the next row's). |
| **NeedsRow** (K5) | `NeedItem{source, tone, title, detail, asOf, area, actionKey}`; `NeedsRow::draw(c, rect, item, clock, self)`; `NeedsRow::hit(rect, x, y)`; `NeedsRow::kHeight` 72 | As `ui-need`: tone bar, title, detail, "since 10:32 . Area", and the action phrase from `needs.h`. The whole row is the target. |
| **Meter** (K5) | `Meter::draw(c, rect, reading, fraction)` returns whether it drew | Only for a real fraction (0 to 1) of a live or stale reading; otherwise draws nothing and returns false, and the screen shows the age or "Unknown". Stale is muted. No indeterminate bar. |
| **Frame** (K5) | `Frame::draw(c, title, Level::One or Two, subtitle = nullptr, subtitleColor)`; `Frame::hit(level, x, y)` returns None, Back or Home; `Frame::content(tabBarHeight)` | The 48 px header on `bar`. Back at the left and Home at the right (88 x 48 each), always in those places. `Level::One` is a top screen: Back is drawn disabled and does not hit. `Level::Two` is one step in. There is no third level. Draw in `content(kTabBarH)` (480 x 224), or `content(0)` without the device's tab bar. |
| **Stepper** (K9) | `Stepper::draw(c, rect, value, unit, canDec, canInc, bg)`; `Stepper::hit(rect, value, canDec, canInc, x, y)` returns None, Dec or Inc | For a number. 48 px keys with the value centred. A null value (unreadable) shows "Unknown" and disables both keys. |
| **Switch** (K9) | `Switch::draw(c, rect, label, SwitchState::Off, On or Unknown, bg)`; `Switch::hit(rect, state, x, y)` | A track, a knob and the word On or Off. Unknown is a hollow track, no knob, "Unknown", and ignores taps. |
| **Picker** (K9) | see below | The one control for a named choice, a colour, or a clock time. |

### Picker

```cpp
struct PickerOption { const char* label; bool hasSwatch = false; uint16_t swatch = 0; };
enum class PickerEvent : uint8_t { None, Chose, Back, Home, Scrolled };
struct PickerResult { PickerEvent event; int index; };

ui::Picker picker("Time zone", options, count, currentIndex /* -1 if unreadable */, kTabBarH);
picker.draw(canvas);                                   // the whole screen except the tab bar
PickerResult r = picker.tap(canvas, x, y);             // Chose(index), Back, Home, Scrolled, or None
picker.failed(index, "no connection to the Pi");       // the save of Chose(index) failed
```

- The title is the setting's name; Back and Home are in their usual places. Options are the caller's array, at most
  `Picker::kMaxOptions` (128), kept alive while the Picker is.
- One option per row, **at least 48 px tall**, label in 16 px text, **never shrunk and never cut**: a long label wraps
  onto more lines and its row grows (up to `kMaxLines` 8 lines). A colour option shows its swatch beside its name.
- The **current choice has a check mark and a wash**, so it is not marked by colour alone.
- Four options per page is the expected layout. A longer list scrolls by pages with **Previous** and **Next** keys
  (at least 48 px, 14 px text, a "2/3" page number between); the list **opens on the page with the current choice**.
- **A tap on an option returns `Chose(index)`**. The app saves it; when it is saved the app closes the Picker and shows
  the new value on the page it came from. `Back` returns `Back` and changes nothing.
- **Failure:** call `failed(index, reason)`. The Picker stays open, that row says "Not saved: reason" in the bad colour,
  and the previous choice keeps its check mark (the Picker's current value only changes if the app builds a new one).
  The next tap clears the message. It never closes itself.
- **Unknown:** with `current = -1` (or an index outside the list) no row is checked, and the title line says "Current
  setting unknown". The first option is never pre-selected.
- A clock time (night mode start and end) is a Picker of times in 15-minute steps, built by the screen: 96 options.
- Test hooks for the screen's own checks: `firstVisible(c)`, `endVisible(c)`, `scrolls(c)`, `rowRect(c, i)`,
  `previousRect(c)`, `nextRect(c)`, `hasFailure()`.

## Using it from the firmware

1. `node scripts/sync.mjs <display repo> --dir assets/ui --display` copies `dist/` including `display/` and its fonts,
   with a `VERSION` file of SHA-256 sums; `verify.mjs` or `verify.py` fails on a hand edit. (Without `--display` the web
   apps get the same copy without the display kit.)
2. Implement `UiCanvas` over the LovyanGFX sprite or panel (about 40 lines; load the five fonts once).
3. Include `display/ui.h`, hold a `ui::Clock` that the screen code refreshes from the RTC, and draw parts into
   rectangles, keeping the `Rect` for the hit-test.

## Proof

`npm run display` compiles `tests/display/harness.cpp` against these headers (`-std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic
-Werror`), runs its checks (hit areas, minimum sizes, the honest states, the Picker cases, text that is never cut), renders
every part in every state to RGB565, and compares with `demo/screens/display/*.png`. `npm run display:update` rewrites
those images on purpose, like `npm run screens`. It runs in `npm test`.

The Mac canvas does not antialias `fillRoundRect` corners, and blends glyphs in 8 bits per channel before rounding to
RGB565; LovyanGFX's corners and text blending can differ by a pixel or a level, so device captures (`/hub/frame.ppm`)
are what the owner accepts.

## Fonts (K3)

`fonts/*.vlw` are Archivo cut from `fonts/archivo-latin-ui.woff2` by `npm run fonts` (`scripts/build-fonts.py`; needs
Pillow, a dev-only dependency of that one script; the files are committed). 200 glyphs each: ASCII, Latin-1 and the
dashes, curly quotes, bullet, ellipsis and minus. Text sizes are weight 500; the readout is weight 650 at 75% width.
